name: Pounce transfer
summary: A drawing on paper is pricked along its lines and dabbed with a bag of charcoal dust, so that dots of the design go onto the surface below.
how: Draw the design at full size on paper.
Prick holes along each line, 2 to 3 mm apart.
Lay the sheet on the surface and dab it with a bag of charcoal or graphite dust.
Paint over the dots; the dust burns away in the kiln or wipes off.

origin.note: Fresco painters transfer cartoons to wet plaster with pounced dots (spolvero).

adoptions.via: Delft tile painters pounce one pattern onto many tiles with a pricked sheet, the spons.
